summary: @servicetitan/ko-bridge preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes bundled obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs". setup.mjs is itself obfuscator.io-style mangled (_0x... identifiers, indirection objects) and downloads Bun v1.3.13 from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases into a temp directory, extracts it, chmods it executable, and invokes it via execFileSync against math_init.js at the tarball root — with no hash or signature check on the downloaded runtime. math_init.js is a 727 KB single-line file tagged `// @bun @bun-cjs` containing a large opcode/string array and mangled identifiers; it is not human-readable and is unrelated to the package's advertised Knockout/React bridge purpose. math_init.js is present in the tarball but is not listed in package.json's files array (which declares only "dist" and "src"), so the payload is smuggled outside the declared publish surface. Installing this package triggers automatic execution of an obfuscated payload of unknown function through a freshly-downloaded second language runtime, evading scanners that only inspect Node-resolved code. The package is published under the @servicetitan scope, consistent with either a compromised publish pipeline or an impersonation package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
